A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EMFormer research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original weather forecasts, typhoon-track predictions, ImageNet-1K classification, ADE20K segmentation and component ablations, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds finetuning controls, longer-horizon loss-ablation results and structural re-parameterization comparisons.

M1.justification: The EMFormer architecture, fused convolution procedure, KV-cache pruning, accumulative finetuning and sinusoidal loss remain unchanged in Section 2 and Algorithms 1–3. LoRA and unpruned variants are added as experimental comparisons, not proposed-method revisions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ERA5 weather forecasting, the same ten 2024 typhoons, ImageNet-1K and ADE20K. The added experiments use existing weather data and forecast horizons; they introduce no distinct task, population or environmental scenario.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds LoRA finetuning and an unpruned accumulative-context variant. New Table 16 evaluates RepVGG and RepLKNet at module and full-model levels. These are targeted comparator additions; existing benchmark baselines and the VA-MoE comparison remain.

E3.justification: New Table 16 introduces a module comparison matched at 9.17M parameters and full-model comparisons using six-year training on 1.4° ERA5. Table 3 expands controls and resource measurements, while Table 14 extends loss evaluation to four and ten days. Existing splits, preprocessing and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing ablation suite gains a direct pruning control and LoRA comparison, longer-horizon tests of selected loss variants, and module-versus-full-model comparisons against re-parameterization methods. Table 14 removes its T850 column. Existing cache-length, balancing-weight, finetuning-step, backbone and window-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The caption of new Table 16 specifies averaging module efficiency over 50 inferences. This adds repeated-measurement information absent from v1, but does not establish additional training seeds, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged. Table 3 adds LoRA and no-pruning outcomes, including ten-day RMSEs of 0.5278 and 0.5153 versus the retained pruned result of 0.5094. Table 14 adds longer-horizon scores and removes T850 entries. New Table 16 reports module latency of 8.9 ms versus 14.3 for RepVGG and 14.5 for RepLKNet, alongside additional forecasting results.

T1.justification: The mathematical statements, equations, Assumption A.1 and appendix proofs are unchanged. Relabeling theorems as propositions does not alter their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and claims about efficiency, temporal consistency and vision-task generalization remain. Although v2 removes the 5.69× speedup phrase from the abstract, the identical claim remains in the introduction and appendix.

C2.justification: Appendix F.4 adds an interpretation of the RepVGG/RepLKNet comparisons: module-level efficiency advantages carry through to full-model forecasting performance. Existing explanations of temporal consistency, cache trade-offs and loss dynamics remain, without new substantive limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository address in the abstract. Existing algorithms, hardware descriptions, hyperparameter tables and supplementary-material descriptions remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access pointer, not the repository's contents or availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ding et al. (2022, RepLKNet) and Shang et al. (2025), and removes Cheon et al. (2024, KARINA), including Table 15's attribution of some data to KARINA. The broader research positioning is retained, with a focused additional comparison against structural re-parameterization methods.

P1.justification: Edits include theorem-to-proposition terminology, revised correspondence and publication text, acknowledgements, the abstract's code pointer and additional discussion in Appendix F.4. Most prose and the section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains grouped rows and resource columns; Table 14 is reorganized around three forecast horizons; and new Table 16 contains two comparison panels. Later tables are renumbered and redistributed across pages. Existing figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added finetuning controls, re-parameterization comparisons and longer-horizon loss tests provide useful support for the retained design, while the code address improves access information. Gains are limited by removed T850 ablation results and unexplained differences between new ten-day EMFormer entries in Tables 14 and 16: Z500 is 756.67 versus 764.51, and U10 is 4.22 versus 4.27 under similarly described six-year settings.
